description: This exists because the audit that produced it was a one-off: a person wondered how far behind the stack was, checked seventeen images by hand, and found swagger-ui two years old and PostgREST two majors back. Nothing would have raised either again. The point of this file is that the CHECK happens on a schedule. Deciding what to merge stays a human job, and several rules below exist to keep it that way.

WHAT A NAIVE CONFIGURATION WOULD GET WRONG HERE, and why packageRules is the long half: the Supabase components are a COORDINATED SET that upstream tests together. Measured against Docker Hub, a member of the set can look outdated when it is exactly the version upstream pins, and bumping it alone would move this stack OFF the tested combination. Renovate cannot read upstream's compose file, so it must not be trusted to propose those individually.

THE DASHBOARD IS THE DELIVERABLE, more than the PRs are. It is one issue listing every available update including the ones deliberately held back, which is exactly the artefact the manual audit produced and then threw away.

SCHEDULING IS MONTHLY, AND THE WORKFLOW CRON IS NOT. Routine currency work opens on the first of the month (the window is the whole day, since the cron that invokes Renovate fires hours after its nominal time and a morning window never matched), because a weekly batch of pull requests is a standing tax on whoever has to read them and the thing being defended against moves over months, not days. The workflow that INVOKES Renovate still runs daily, and that is deliberate rather than sloppy: Renovate can only act while the process is running, so a monthly cron would silently make vulnerabilityAlerts monthly too -- and those are supposed to ignore the schedule entirely. Daily invocation plus a monthly window means routine noise once a month and a security advisory picked up within a day. A release must be three days old before it becomes a PR, so one that is pulled within days never does; the Supabase set and the historian wait seven, and vulnerability alerts wait for nothing.

packageRules.description: Images built from this repository. The tag is set at deploy time and is empty in values.yaml, so there is no upstream to track.

EVERY IMAGE IS NAMED IN NOTICE.md AT ITS TAG, with its licence read at that tag, and check-image-licences fails a pull request that moves a pin and not the notice. Renovate cannot read a licence, so an image pull request is finished by hand.
prBodyNotes: Before merging: read the new image's licence (in the image for NOTICE.md's *Verified from the pinned image* rows, at the upstream tag for the others) and name the tag in `NOTICE.md`, and in `licenses/README.md` where a copied licence was read at it. `node scripts/check-image-licences.mjs` fails until it does. `docs/architecture.md`'s image table names the tag too.

packageRules.description: THE COORDINATED SET. One PR or none: these move together upstream and are tested together, and the correct target is usually upstream Supabase's own pin rather than the newest tag. dependencyDashboardApproval means Renovate lists them and waits to be asked, because the decision needs a person to compare against supabase/supabase docker/docker-compose.yml. See issue #49.

THE DENO THAT RESOLVES THE EDGE FUNCTIONS is the Deno supabase/edge-runtime embeds (`edge-runtime --version`), not the newest: the functions image's `modules` stage and the top-level constraints.deno (which the deno manager maintains supabase/functions/deno.lock with) both name it, and a lock written by another Deno can be a format the build cannot read. It moves by hand when edge-runtime does.
The same Deno, in constraints.deno above. The renovate-config manager reads that pin as a dependency of this file and proposes moving it to the newest Deno; it moves with edge-runtime, by hand.
The historian. Not grouped with anything: a patch bump is usually safe and is still the one change that can take the telemetry store with it.
prBodyNotes: Before merging: set `$timescaledbVersion` in `deploy/helm/aber/templates/jobs/timescaledb-maintenance.yaml` to the new TimescaleDB version, and the tag in `.github/rehearsal-values.yaml` to the new image. The maintenance hook waits for the historian to offer that version, and `node scripts/check-docs-drift.mjs` fails until both match the Dockerfile.

packageRules.description: THE BROKER. Docker Hub publishes Mosquitto 2.1 and later only under `-alpine` tags, and Renovate keeps a tag suffix as its own stream, so the unsuffixed 2.0.22 pin was never offered 2.1. This keeps proposals to exact `X.Y.Z-alpine` tags, never the floating `2.1-alpine`. One PR moves both pins, values.yaml and gateway-credential/Dockerfile, which check-docs-drift holds together because the credential image's mosquitto_passwd and mosquitto_rr must be the broker's own. A minor release has changed mosquitto_passwd's output before, so run `node scripts/check-broker-config.mjs` on the branch before merging.

GRAFANA. grafana.ini disables every bundled backend datasource plugin no provisioned datasource uses, and check-docs-drift fails while the chart pins a tag other than the one grafana/README.md's list of bundled plugins was read from. A new image can bundle a plugin the old one did not, so the pull request is finished by hand: the command and the steps are in grafana/README.md, Bundled plugins. A release waits seven days, as the broker's and the historian's do.
prBodyNotes: Before merging: read the new image's bundled datasource plugins into `grafana/README.md` (Bundled plugins) and `disable_plugins` in `grafana/grafana.ini`. `node scripts/check-docs-drift.mjs` fails until they name this tag.

packageRules.description: A major version is a reading task before it is a merge task. Held on the dashboard so it is proposed deliberately -- Kong 3.0, for one, silently switched off every per-service Prometheus metric while leaving the scrape target green.
A Python minor is a new interpreter, and is held like a major. Compiled wheels lag its release: on python 3.15, psycopg2-binary had none and the ingestion image's build failed.
Workflow actions: one PR, since they are independent of everything the stack runs.
